subject: Request: Temporary SLA Exception & Operational Impact Assessment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@opalcloud.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: OpalCloud Legal <contracts@opalcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLA exception request for batch inference workload

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed internally, OpalCloud is planning a phased migration of a high-volume batched inference job into Redwood Dedicated starting Q3. The workload has predictable daily spikes (3–4 hours) where latency SLOs can slip because of synchronous batching across many models.

Before we proceed to procurement, legal asked us to request a limited SLA exception for the first 90 days of the pilot. High-level ask:
- Allow a temporary monthly uptime floor of 98.0% (vs standard 99.9%) for the pilot window.
- Cap monthly service credits at a fixed amount ($10k) during the pilot period.
- Include opt-in telemetry export (KV cache hit rates + request traces) to help root cause.

Attached is the Opal_SLA_Request.pdf with sample traffic curves and May downtime log. Can Redwood provide a proposed scoped amendment and any operational requirements (engine config, recommended batching settings) you need?

Goal is to lock pilot terms by next week so procurement can issue the PO.

Best,
Samir
Head of Infrastructure, OpalCloud
[Attachment: Opal_SLA_Request.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)]
[Attachment: downtime_log_May.csv (text/csv, 48KB)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@opalcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA exception request for batch inference workload

Samir —

Appreciate the detail and the sample logs. Quick response while I pull engineering: we can accommodate a 90-day pilot exception but need to coordinate engineering guardrails and an adjusted credit schedule so we preserve safety for other tenants. Proposed next steps from Redwood:

1) Operational checklist (we'll share an engineering runbook):
   - Dedicated pool pinning during spike windows
   - Autoscale thresholds and pre-warming policy
   - Recommended batching window and max batch size per model
   - Prefix KV-cache tuning and TTLs
2) Drafted amendment (short form) with:
   - Pilot uptime floor: 98.0% (90-day window)
   - Fixed monthly credit cap: $10,000 for months 1–3
   - Telemetry export: limited to operational metrics; PII not shared; retention 30 days
3) Legal redlines: looped in Laura and Ben (cc).

I'll have a one-page amendment and runbook draft by end of day tomorrow. Can we schedule a 30-min alignment call Thursday morning (your time)?

Thanks,
Avery
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: (none)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Temporary SLA exception request for batch inference workload

Avery / Ben —

Forwarding Samir's request. Quick legal read:
- Pilot cap at $10k is fine but we should make credits the exclusive remedy for SLA failures during the pilot period. No broader indemnity carveouts.
- Telemetry export: require data processing addendum (DPA) language — limit fields and enforce retention.
- Suggest adding a clause: Redwood may temporarily prioritize other customers if the pilot causes systemic degradation; Opal will be notified 48 hours in advance of any forced throttling.

Ben — please prepare a redline (short amendment) that includes the exclusive-remedy language and DPA pointers. Also confirm whether the 48-hour notice clause is operationally feasible.

—Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_SLA_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 34KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@opalcloud.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed short amendment for 90-day pilot (OpalCloud)

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short amendment draft (redline) that reflects the pilot terms. Highlights:
- Uptime floor: 98.0% for months 1–3 of the pilot.
- Credits: fixed cap of $10,000/month; credits calculated pro-rata based on downtime percentage.
- Exclusive remedy: credits are sole monetary remedy for SLA failures in pilot window.
- Telemetry: operational metrics export with a DPA addendum; limited to non-PII metrics and 30-day retention.
- Operational carve: Redwood may throttle or re-route traffic during platform-wide incidents; we will notify Opal 48 hours prior where feasible.

Operational note (Avery): engineering confirmed pre-warm + scaling policy can be implemented, but they asked for: a rolling restart blackout window (2 hours/week) where Opal agrees to not schedule heavy migrations.

Samir — can you confirm acceptance of the above points and whether your legal team wants any alternate DPA language? If good, we'll send the DocuSign envelope and loop procurement.

Best,
Ben
Sr. Commercial Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_SLA_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 34KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@opalcloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed short amendment for 90-day pilot (OpalCloud)

Ben / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. OpalCloud is comfortable with the amendment as drafted with two small asks:
1) Replace "48 hours prior where feasible" notification with "48 hours prior in non-emergency scenarios" so we can request failover validation.
2) Clarify the rolling restart blackout window timing: we prefer the blackout to be scheduled in UTC 02:00–04:00 (Opal local low traffic) and allow a one-time exception in month 2 for a migration.

If you can incorporate those tweaks, Opal legal will sign and we'll push the PO. We also confirm we accept the $10k/month credit cap for months 1–3.

Thanks — looking forward to the runbook and DocuSign.

Samir
Head of Infrastructure, OpalCloud
[Attachment: (none)]
